Wikipedia coverage of CyrusOne states the company purchased 40 acres in Loudoun County in June 2016 for data center construction. CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, went public in 2013, and was taken private in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts and Global Infrastructure Partners acquired it for 15 billion dollars. reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus occupies 420,000 square feet across three connected facilities in Loudoun County, Virginia, and publishes 44 megawatts of IT capacity. At 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, 44 megawatts of IT load is roughly 1,100 racks. The campus certifies for financial services compliance, healthcare data handling, federal systems, and general enterprise standards, indicating readiness for regulated workloads but not disclosing what tenants it currently serves.

Sterling ranks 10th among Virginia's 23 facilities with published power capacity, holding 3.2 percent of the state's 1,375 megawatts of disclosed supply. Virginia hosts 326 mapped data centers in total, though the vast majority publish no figures. The Sterling campus is one of the larger disclosed installations in a state whose Ashburn corridor concentrates significant national capacity.

The operator, CyrusOne, was taken private in 2022 by KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners for fifteen billion dollars. Whether the Sterling campus will expand beyond its current published footprint is not stated. Total capacity in megawatts, not just IT load, is not published.
